blocks.text: קְרוֹבוֹת לְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
uncertainties: Header of the printed page. Page number 54 is printed on both sides.

blocks.text: לַזָּר חֲרָדָה. וְחִלְּלָה מְלוּכָה: לָחֲצָה בְּנֵי מֶלֶךְ. וּפָצָה לְעֵין מֶלֶךְ. מִי לִי בְּרֹק מֶלֶךְ: יָהֲרָה בְּכֵס מֶלֶךְ. זוּלָתִי אֵין מֶלֶךְ. אֲנִי וְאַפְסִי מֶלֶךְ:
uncertainties: This continues from the previous page with no opening siglum.
The last word of line 1, 'וּפָצָה', sits at the margin. It could also be 'וּפָצְתָה'. I read four letters.
'בְּרֹק': the third letter looks like it has a ק descender. The English ('Who is in heaven my king') suggests a word like 'בָּרוּם'. This is a possible typo. Please check the scan.
'לָחֲצָה': I read qamats under the lamed and hataf-patah under the het.

blocks.text: רָם עַל כָּל־מֶלֶךְ. תַּגְעִילֶנָּה מִמֶּלֶךְ. וּלְךָ תָּשִׁיב מְלוּכָה:
uncertainties: 'מִמֶּלֶךְ': the first letter could be מ or כ. The English 'remove from it the rank of king' supports מ.
'תַּגְעִילֶנָּה': I am not sure whether the nun has a dagesh.
The superscript siglum before 'רָם'. It is presumably the hazzan.

blocks.text: תָּעִיר וְתָרִיעַ. לְהַכְרִית כָּל מֵרִיעַ. וְתִתְקַדֵּשׁ בְּיוֹדְעֵי לְהָרִיעַ. קָדוֹשׁ:
uncertainties: Printed in smaller type with no speaker siglum. The recitation role is not marked.
Probably 'hazzan and congregation'.

blocks.text: מֶלֶךְ מְמַלֵּט מֵרָעָה. לְיוֹדְעֵי תְרוּעָה. הָאֵל קָדוֹשׁ:
uncertainties: I read 'תְרוּעָה' with no dagesh visible in the tav.

blocks.text: מֶלֶךְ זוֹכֵר אֲחוּז קֶרֶן. לְתוֹקְעֵי לְךָ הַיּוֹם בְּקֶרֶן. נוֹרָא וְקָדוֹשׁ:

uncertainties: The first word is small and unclear. It looks like 'חזן' or 'מִן'. The English has 'On Sabbath.' Please check the scan. Only 'שַׁבָּת.' is certain.

blocks.text: וְרָשַׁם בְּחֹק דַּת הֶגְיוֹנִי. בְּכָל שָׁנָה וְשָׁנָה לִזְכּוֹר זִכְרוֹנִי.
uncertainties: Siglum ח׳ (hazzan).
Siglum ק׳ (congregation).
Printed in smaller type after the stanza. It looks like a catchword or cue to another text, not part of this stanza. Its exact function is unclear.

blocks.text: זֶבַח קֹדֶשׁ כְּהֻכְשַׁר אָז בְּעֵינָיו. רִגֵּל תְּמוּרָתוֹ אַיִל לְהַקְרִיב לְפָנָיו.
uncertainties: Siglum ח׳.
'רִגֵּל': the vowel under the resh is unclear. It could be 'רֶגֶל'. I read a dagesh in the gimel.
Siglum ק׳.

blocks.text: חִכֵּם חֲנִיטָיו לִתְקוֹעַ בְּזֶה חֹדֶשׁ. יוֹם זֶה אִם יִקָּרֶה בַּשַּׁבָּת קֹדֶשׁ.
uncertainties: Siglum ח׳.
'יִקָּרֶה': the pointing under the kof is unclear. It could be 'יִקְרֶה'.
Siglum ק׳ is printed right against the word.

blocks.text: טִבְעוֹ אִם בְּחֹל יְבוֹאֲכֶם. צַוּוּ לִתְקוֹעַ בְּכָל גְּבוּלְכֶם.
uncertainties: Siglum ח׳ is printed right against the word.
'צַוּוּ': the vowel under the tsadi could be patah or hiriq ('צִוּוּ').
Siglum ק׳.
Small-type catchword or cue at the end of the paragraph.

blocks.text: יָרוּם צוּר יִשְׁעִי בְּפִי כָּל־אֻמִּים. חֲשׂוֹף זְרוֹעֲךָ לְהוֹשִׁיעַ מִמִּתְקוֹמְמִים.
uncertainties: Siglum ח׳.
Siglum ק׳.

blocks.text: כְּהִגָּלוֹתְךָ לְעֵין כֹּל שִׁכְנְךָ לְהִוָּעֵד. קְהִלּוֹת וּרְבָבוֹת בְּפִימוֹ לְהָעֵד.
uncertainties: Siglum ח׳.
'כֹּל' or 'כָּל': the vowel is unclear.
Siglum ק׳. It ends with a period, not a sof-pasuq colon, as printed.

blocks.text: לְךָ יָאֲתָה כָּבוֹד (נ״א מַלְכוּת) וָעֹז הֲגוּיִם. חֶלֶד וְכָל שׁוֹכְנֶיהָ וְכָל הָאִיִּים.
uncertainties: Siglum ח׳.
The parenthesis is a printed alternative reading: 'נ״א מַלְכוּת' (another version reads מלכות instead of כבוד). The siglum inside it could be 'כ״א'; I read 'נ״א'.
'הֲגוּיִם' is as printed (meaning 'spoken'). Compare 'הַגּוֹיִם' later on the page. I do not think it is a typo.
This is the same alternative that appears inline in the block above, recorded separately.
Siglum ק׳.
Small-type catchword or cue at the end of the page.

blocks.text: Morning Prayer for the New Year

and desecrated the realm of God. It oppressed the King's children (Israel) and said in the sight of the King: "Who is in heaven my king?". There is boasting from the royal throne: "There is no king besides me, I alone am king". O Thou who art exalted above all kings, remove from it the rank of king, so that the kingdom may return to Thee.
uncertainties: Quotation marks and the '?".' punctuation are copied as printed.

blocks.text: Thou dost rise and let the trumpet sound to destroy every evil doer, and Thou art sanctified by those who know how to sound the Teruah, Holy One.
O King, Thou savest from misfortune those who understand Teruah, Holy God.
uncertainties: 'un-derstand' is hyphenated across a line break in print.
A stray dot is printed between מלך and 'O'.

blocks.text: O King, Thou dost remember him (Isaac) who was caught by the horn (the ram) on behalf of those who blow the horn before Thee today, O awe-inspiring and Holy One!

uncertainties: Printed in italics.

blocks.text: He has inscribed my thoughts through a statute of the faith so as to remember me year by year, for a remembrance in the sanctuary of the Lord.
uncertainties: No Hebrew linkage word is printed before this paragraph.

blocks.text: When the holy sacrifice (Isaac) once found favour in His eyes, He allowed a ram to be sacrificed in his stead, which was later caught with his horns in the thicket. He taught the descendants of (Isaac) to blow the Shofar on this new moon; but if this day falls on a Sabbath, then the mere mention of Teruah is a sacred proclamation. When it falls on a weekday for you, let it be blown in all your regions, let it be a day of Teruah for you.
uncertainties: This paragraph covers the Hebrew stanzas זבח, חכם and טבעו. No separate linkage words are printed for חכם or טבעו.

blocks.text: Exalted is the rock of my salvation in the mouths of all peoples. Expose Thine arm to help us against adversaries, Thy realm is a realm of all eternity. When Thou revealest Thyself before all eyes to visit once again Thy dwelling place, congregations in their myriads will proclaim aloud: The Lord shall reign for ever and ever. Becoming to Thee is honour and the acknowledgment of might pronounced by the earth and its inhabitants and all the isles: who does not fear Thee, King of the nations.
uncertainties: The Hebrew alternative (נ״א מלכות) is not reflected in the English.

notes: No cantillation, rafe or meteg marks could be identified on s136.
Sigla on s136: ח׳ = hazzan, ק׳ = congregation (superscript), and חו״ק twice before the מלך lines. The תעיר line is in smaller type and has no siglum.

The small-type words שׁוֹמְרֵי מִצְוֹתָיו. / שַׁפְּרוּ. / שִׁבְטֵי. come at the ends of the Sabbath and ירום paragraphs. I have classified them as cue or catchword linkages, not prayer text. They probably point to alternative or weekday text. They do not appear in the English.
Possible source typo: 'בְּרֹק' in 'מִי לִי בְּרֹק מֶלֶךְ'. The English 'in heaven' suggests something like 'בָּרוּם'. I am not confident about the reading, so check the original before correcting.
The bands overlap: each repeated line was counted only once.
The Sabbath rubric's first word is uncertain. Only 'שַׁבָּת.' is read with confidence.
